hyperedges.label: LoRA Ecosystem: Vanilla to Adaptive to Generated
hyperedges.rationale: These four concepts form a progression in LoRA sophistication: vanilla LoRA (uniform low-rank) -> asymmetry insight (A/B play different roles) -> AdaLoRA (adaptive rank via SVD importance) -> DnD (zero-shot LoRA generation from prompts). Each stage addresses a limitation of the previous.

hyperedges.label: Weight Space Composition Triangle
hyperedges.rationale: These papers and concepts form a coherent research program on composing models in weight space: task arithmetic establishes the framework and identifies disentanglement as prerequisite; TIES-Merging fixes sign conflicts that break naive composition; AWE adaptively tunes interpolation for few-shot settings. Together they advance the thesis that weight space supports systematic model combination.

hyperedges.label: Symmetry-Aware Architecture Understanding
hyperedges.rationale: These concepts and papers form a theory-to-application chain: functional symmetries provide the abstract theory of what transformations preserve neural network behavior; neural DAG automorphisms formalize these symmetries for arbitrary architectures; parameter graphs provide the practical representation; GMN implements equivariant processing; the survey synthesizes these into the WSU component of its taxonomy.

hyperedges.label: LoRA symmetry handling for weight-space generation
hyperedges.description: LoRA's GL_r symmetry and permutation symmetry are the core obstacles to using LoRA weights as data; multiplicative LoRA with asymmetric masking addresses both internal and external symmetries to produce structured, learnable weight spaces.

hyperedges.label: Multi-task LoRA generation via task vectors and CVAE
hyperedges.description: ICM-LoRA's three-stage pipeline: task vectors condition the CVAE, which is trained via in-context meta-learning to capture cross-task correlations; together they enable single-generator multi-task LoRA parameter synthesis.

hyperedges.label: Weight-space hidden state enables gradient-free adaptation
hyperedges.description: WARP's weight-space linear RNN unifies the fast weight programmer paradigm with weight-space learning: the auxiliary network's weights serve as the hidden state, updated via linear recurrence with input differences, enabling gradient-free test-time adaptation.

nodes.label: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
nodes.author: Gabriel Ilharco, Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Mitchell Wortsman, Suchin Gururangan, Ludwig Schmidt, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Ali Farhadi

nodes.label: Task Vector
nodes.rationale: A task vector is obtained by subtracting pre-trained model weights from fine-tuned model weights, defining a direction in weight space. Arithmetic operations (negation, addition, analogy composition) on task vectors steer model behavior without extra inference cost, because operations are purely element-wise on weights.

nodes.label: Task Arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Negating a task vector unlearns a task; adding vectors creates multi-task models; forming analogies transfers knowledge to unseen tasks. Chosen because it requires no additional data or training and has zero inference latency overhead.

nodes.label: Weight Interpolation
nodes.rationale: Prior work on weight interpolation motivated the task vector construction. Linear interpolation between model weights can maintain or improve performance, underpinning the additive structure exploited by task arithmetic.

nodes.label: Weights2Weights: Interpreting the Weight Space of Customized Diffusion Models
nodes.author: Amil Dravid, Yossi Gandelsman, Kuan-Chieh Wang, Alexei A. Efros, Rameen Abdal, Gordon Wetzstein, Kfir Aberman
nodes.norm_label: weights2weights: interpreting the weight space of customized diffusion models

nodes.label: weights2weights (w2w) Space
nodes.rationale: A PCA-derived subspace over 60k+ LoRA fine-tuned diffusion model weights, one model per identity, functions as a meta-latent space. Sampling from it yields new identity-encoding models; linear directions correspond to semantic edits. LoRA is used to reduce dimensionality before PCA, making the manifold tractable.

nodes.label: Meta-Latent Space over Model Weights
nodes.rationale: Unlike GAN latent spaces that control individual images, the w2w meta-latent space controls the model itself, enabling consistent multi-image generation for a subject. This motivates treating model weights as data points in a learnable generative space.

nodes.label: ORAL: Prompting Your Large-Scale LoRAs via Conditional Recurrent Diffusion
nodes.author: Rana Muhammad Shahroz Khan, Pingzhi Li, Kai Wang, Dongwen Tang, Tianlong Chen
nodes.norm_label: oral: prompting your large-scale loras via conditional recurrent diffusion

nodes.label: Conditional Recurrent Diffusion for LoRA Generation
nodes.rationale: ORAL uses a recurrent diffusion backbone (from RPG) augmented with a novel conditioning mechanism encoding model architecture and textual task specifications. This achieves simultaneous scalability (up to 7B parameter LLMs), controllability (task-specific generation), and portability (transfer to evolving base models without retraining) — properties no prior method achieved together.
nodes.norm_label: conditional recurrent diffusion for lora generation

nodes.label: Neural Network Parameter Generation
nodes.rationale: Parameter generation treats neural network weights as a distinct modality to synthesize directly, offering an alternative to traditional training. Prior work (P-Diff, Cond P-Diff, RPG) each solved only a subset of scalability/controllability/portability.

nodes.label: Knowledge Is a Region in Weight Space for Finetuned Language Models
nodes.author: Almog Gueta, Elad Venezian, Colin Raffel, Noam Slonim, Yoav Katz, Leshem Choshen
nodes.norm_label: knowledge is a region in weight space for finetuned language models

nodes.label: Knowledge Region in Weight Space
nodes.rationale: Fine-tuned models optimized for high performance cluster in well-defined, linearly connected regions of weight space. Any model within a region also performs well. The center of such a region outperforms individual fine-tuned models on average, suggesting the best models may not lie at region edges (where gradient-based fine-tuning typically ends).

nodes.label: Linear Mode Connectivity
nodes.rationale: Models fine-tuned on the same dataset are linearly connected in weight space — the convex hull between them forms a connected low-loss basin. This extends the linear connectivity result of Entezari et al. to a full bounded convex region, not just a line.

nodes.label: Equivariant Deep Weight Space Alignment (Deep-Align / DWSNets)
nodes.author: Aviv Navon, Aviv Shamsian, Ethan Fetaya, Gal Chechik, Nadav Dym, Haggai Maron
nodes.norm_label: equivariant deep weight space alignment (deep-align / dwsnets)

nodes.label: Deep-Align Framework
nodes.rationale: A learning-based weight alignment method using DWSNets with Siamese architecture. Alignment is reduced to a feedforward pass rather than iterative optimization (NP-hard in general). Equivariance design reduces training set size requirements and enables efficient inference.

nodes.label: Permutation Symmetry of Neural Networks
nodes.rationale: Deep networks maintain function under permutations of weights, making naive weight averaging or distance computation meaningless without alignment. This symmetry motivates equivariant architectures that respect it by design.

nodes.label: Weight Alignment
nodes.rationale: Finding optimal permutations between two networks' weight matrices to make them comparable. Critical for model merging, loss landscape study, and federated learning. NP-hard in general; prior work uses relaxed optimization.

nodes.label: Predicting Trends in the Quality of State-of-the-Art Neural Networks without Access to Training or Testing Data
nodes.author: Charles H. Martin, Tongsu Peng, Michael W. Mahoney
nodes.norm_label: predicting trends in the quality of state-of-the-art neural networks without access to training or testing data

nodes.label: Power Law (Heavy-Tailed) Metrics for Model Quality
nodes.rationale: PL-based metrics (weighted alpha, alpha-norm) derived from eigenvalue power-law fits outperform norm-based metrics for predicting model quality without training/test data. They can distinguish well-trained vs. poorly-trained models where norms fail (Scale Collapse). Based on Theory of Heavy-Tailed Self Regularization.
nodes.norm_label: power law (heavy-tailed) metrics for model quality

nodes.label: WeightWatcher Tool
nodes.rationale: A publicly available tool (v0.2.7) used to compute norm- and PL-based weight matrix metrics on pretrained models without access to training data.

nodes.label: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
nodes.author: Armen Aghajanyan, Luke Zettlemoyer, Sonal Gupta
nodes.norm_label: intrinsic dimensionality explains the effectiveness of language model fine-tuning

nodes.label: Intrinsic Dimension of Fine-Tuning
nodes.rationale: The minimum number of parameters needed to achieve ~90% of full fine-tuning performance. Pre-training implicitly minimizes this intrinsic dimension, and larger models tend to have lower intrinsic dimension, directly motivating low-rank adaptation approaches like LoRA. RoBERTa can be fine-tuned with only 200 parameters projected back to full space.

nodes.label: Structure-Aware Intrinsic Dimension (SAID)
nodes.rationale: An extension of intrinsic dimension measurement that incorporates layer-wise scaling parameters. Addresses the limitation of layer-unaware DID by allowing different layers to contribute differently to the subspace optimization, reflecting that attention layers specialize separately.

nodes.label: LoRAGen: Structure-Aware Weight Space Learning for LoRA Generation
nodes.author: Hao Huang, Jingtao Ding, Mengqi Liao, Xin Wang, Jinyang Ban, Yuan Yuan, Huaiyu Wan, Yong Li
nodes.norm_label: loragen: structure-aware weight space learning for lora generation

nodes.label: LoRAGen Method
nodes.rationale: Generates LoRA parameters from natural language task descriptions using a latent diffusion model. Addresses non-uniqueness of low-rank decomposition by supervising on full adaptation matrix (not A/B matrices directly). Uses a module-aware Mix-of-Experts decoder to handle heterogeneous weight distributions across Transformer modules.

nodes.label: Non-Uniqueness of Low-Rank Decomposition
nodes.rationale: For any invertible R, (BR)(R^{-1}A) yields the same full adaptation matrix ΔW. Supervising on A,B directly is sensitive to arbitrary rescalings/rotations; supervising on ΔW avoids this ambiguity and improves generalization.

nodes.label: Module-Aware Mix-of-Experts (MoE) Decoder
nodes.rationale: Different Transformer modules (encoder self-attention, decoder self-attention, cross-attention) have systematically different spectral-entropy distributions. A shared decoder cannot model this heterogeneity; routing to module-specialized experts with structural embeddings addresses it.

nodes.label: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT (ROME)
nodes.author: Kevin Meng, David Bau, Alex Andonian, Yonatan Belinkov
nodes.norm_label: locating and editing factual associations in gpt (rome)

nodes.label: Rank-One Model Editing (ROME)
nodes.rationale: Modifies feed-forward weights at specific middle-layer MLP modules to update factual associations. Uses causal mediation analysis to locate decisive neuron activations. Achieves specificity and generalization simultaneously, unlike fine-tuning or interpretability-based alternatives.

nodes.label: Causal Mediation Analysis for Knowledge Localization
nodes.rationale: Identifies which internal hidden states causally mediate factual predictions by corrupting subject tokens and restoring activations layer by layer. Reveals that middle-layer MLP modules at subject-last-token positions are decisive, not attention layers.
nodes.norm_label: causal mediation analysis for knowledge localization

nodes.label: Mid-Layer MLP Modules as Factual Association Storage
nodes.rationale: Factual associations in GPT are stored in localized, directly-editable computations within mid-layer feed-forward modules, not distributed across all layers, enabling targeted weight edits.
nodes.norm_label: mid-layer mlp modules as factual association storage

nodes.label: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
nodes.author: Edward Hu, Yelong Shen, Phillip Wallis, Zeyuan Allen-Zhu, Yuanzhi Li, Shean Wang, Lu Wang, Weizhu Chen
nodes.norm_label: lora: low-rank adaptation of large language models

nodes.label: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
nodes.rationale: Freezes pre-trained weights and injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices (ΔW=BA) into Transformer layers. Motivated by the low intrinsic dimension of fine-tuning (Aghajanyan et al., 2020; Li et al., 2018). Reduces trainable parameters by ~10,000x vs GPT-3 full fine-tuning with no inference latency since ΔW can be merged at deploy time.

nodes.label: Rank Deficiency in Weight Updates
nodes.rationale: The hypothesis that weight changes during adaptation have low intrinsic rank justifies LoRA. Even rank r=1 or r=2 suffices for GPT-3 adaptation (d=12288), confirming the low-rank structure of adaptation deltas.

nodes.label: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
nodes.author: Dan Biderman, Jacob Portes, Jose Javier Gonzalez Ortiz, Mansheej Paul, Philip Greengard, Connor Jennings, Daniel King, Sam Havens, Vitaliy Chiley, Jonathan Frankle, Cody Blakeney, John P. Cunningham
nodes.norm_label: lora learns less and forgets less

nodes.label: LoRA Learning-Forgetting Tradeoff
nodes.rationale: LoRA substantially underperforms full fine-tuning in continued pretraining but forgets less of source domain capabilities. The constrained low-rank update acts as an implicit regularizer stronger than dropout or weight decay. Full fine-tuning produces high-rank perturbations (10-100x typical LoRA rank), explaining the performance gap in challenging domains like code and math.

nodes.label: High-Rank Weight Perturbations in Full Fine-Tuning
nodes.rationale: SVD analysis reveals full fine-tuning produces perturbations with rank 10-100x higher than typical LoRA configurations, challenging the low-rank hypothesis that motivated LoRA in difficult domains like code/math while barely changing the spectrum of base weight matrices.
nodes.norm_label: high-rank weight perturbations in full fine-tuning

nodes.label: Self-Supervised Representation Learning on Neural Network Weights for Model Characteristic Prediction
nodes.author: Konstantin Schürholt, Dimche Kostadinov, Damian Borth
nodes.norm_label: self-supervised representation learning on neural network weights for model characteristic prediction

nodes.label: Hyper-Representations of Neural Network Weights
nodes.rationale: SSL (reconstruction + contrastive) applied to populations of trained NNs (model zoos) to learn task-agnostic latent representations. Domain-specific augmentations (permutation, erasing, noise) are critical; permutation augmentation exploits weight-space symmetries and creates near-free valid NN samples for contrastive pairs.

nodes.label: Model Zoo
nodes.rationale: A dataset of trained neural networks with diverse configurations (data, hyperparameters, architecture). Serves as the training corpus for learning hyper-representations. Seed variation within a model zoo adds beneficial diversity for recovering model properties.

nodes.label: Permutation Augmentation for Neural Network Weights
nodes.rationale: Permuting incoming/outgoing weights of a neuron preserves the network's mapping exactly. This creates valid augmented samples at near-zero cost (each layer with N neurons has N! permutations) and exploits structural symmetry as an inductive bias for contrastive learning.
nodes.norm_label: permutation augmentation for neural network weights

attributes.rationale: Identifies a fundamental asymmetry in how the two LoRA matrices contribute to fine-tuning, with practical implications for PEFT efficiency and generalization

attributes.rationale: Identifies that parameter interference (sign conflicts, redundant low-magnitude updates) is the primary failure mode of naive model merging and provides a principled solution

attributes.rationale: Solves the open problem of extending deep weight space networks to architectures with weight sharing by encoding parameters as graph edges rather than nodes

attributes.formulation: W = W0 + BA, where B in R^{d x r}, A in R^{r x k}, r << min(d,k)

attributes.requirement: Weight disentanglement in pre-trained model for arithmetic to work
attributes.rationale: Treats fine-tuned weight deltas as geometric objects supporting arithmetic composition

attributes.definition: Distinct directions in weight space govern separate localized regions in function space
attributes.origin: Emergent property of pre-training; absent at random initialization
attributes.rationale: Mechanistic prerequisite for task arithmetic: if weight directions are not disentangled, task vector composition causes interference

attributes.formulation: f_lin(x; theta0+tau) = f(x; theta0) + tau^T * grad_theta f(x; theta0)
attributes.key_property: Converts nonlinear model to linear in weight perturbations around theta0
attributes.effect_on_arithmetic: Improves task arithmetic by amplifying weight disentanglement
attributes.caveat: Does NOT improve task arithmetic because of linearization per se, but because it amplifies disentanglement
attributes.rationale: First-order Taylor expansion of model enables analysis via neural tangent kernel theory

attributes.formulation: Delta_W = P * Lambda * Q, where P,Q orthogonal, Lambda diagonal (singular values)
attributes.pruning: Set lambda_i = 0 for unimportant singular values; global budget scheduler decays from 1.5x to target rank
attributes.rationale: SVD form provides natural importance measure (singular values) for adaptive rank allocation without computing full SVD

attributes.awe_extension: AWE infers optimal alpha from k-shots using log-linear curve fitting
attributes.rationale: Linear interpolation in weight space between zero-shot and fine-tuned models maintains zero-shot generalization while gaining task accuracy

attributes.training_objective: MSE loss between generated and original tokenized checkpoints

attributes.wsr: Weight Space Representation: model-based (DWSNets, NFN, UNF, GMN, Scale-GMN) and model-free (ProbLog, ProbeX)

attributes.rationale: Provides unified conceptual framework for the emerging field of treating neural network weights as data

attributes.step1_trim: Keep top-k% parameters in task vector tau_t by magnitude; set rest to 0
attributes.step2_elect: gamma_m = sgn(sum_t tau_hat_t); elect sign with greatest total parameter mass
attributes.step3_disjoint_merge: Average only parameters whose sign agrees with elected sign gamma_m
attributes.rationale: Addresses two sources of merging interference: redundant low-magnitude parameters (step 1) and conflicting gradient directions (steps 2-3)

attributes.definition: Graph representation where each model parameter corresponds to exactly one edge
attributes.vs_computation_graphs: Computation graphs have one parameter appearing as many edges in weight-sharing layers; parameter graphs avoid this
attributes.bias_nodes: Bias parameters represented as edges from special bias nodes to layer neurons
attributes.advantage: More compact and efficient for weight-sharing architectures (CNNs, attention)
attributes.rationale: Key innovation enabling GNNs to process diverse neural architectures equivariantly without the redundancy of computation graphs

attributes.definition: Graph automorphisms of the parameter DAG that correspond to functional symmetries of the neural network

attributes.gmn_equivariance: Graph Metanetworks are equivariant to these automorphisms by construction via GNN message passing
attributes.rationale: Provides the correct symmetry group for processing neural network parameters as graph-structured data

attributes.goal: Combine multiple fine-tuned models into single model without retraining
attributes.rationale: Enables knowledge consolidation from multiple specialized models without access to original training data

attributes.invariance: Weight transformation leaves network function unchanged (e.g., neuron permutation)
attributes.equivariance: Weight transformation induces predictable change in network function output
attributes.rationale: Understanding weight space symmetries is prerequisite for building architecture-aware metanetworks

attributes.definition: Neural networks that generate weights for other neural networks
attributes.conditioning: Can be conditioned on task description, architecture spec, or other metadata
attributes.rationale: Enables amortized weight generation, avoiding expensive per-task fine-tuning

attributes.goal: Adapt pre-trained models to new tasks by updating only a small subset of parameters
attributes.advantage: Reduces memory, compute, and storage costs for model adaptation
attributes.rationale: Critical for making LLM adaptation practical at scale

attributes.relevance: Primary testbed for task arithmetic, AWE, and TIES-Merging experiments

attributes.effect: Averaging conflicting parameters reduces their magnitudes, potentially canceling beneficial updates

attributes.rationale: Key source of interference when naively merging task vectors via simple averaging

nodes.label: In-Context Meta LoRA Generation (ICM-LoRA)
nodes.author: Yihua Shao, Minxi Yan, Yang Liu, Siyu Chen, Wenjie Chen, Xinwei Long, Ziyang Yan, Lei Li, Chenyu Zhang, Nicu Sebe, Hao Tang, Yan Wang, Hao Zhao, Mengzhu Wang, Jingcai Guo

nodes.label: ICM-LoRA Framework
nodes.rationale: Proposes a Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) trained on all tasks simultaneously to generate task-specific LoRA weights conditioned on task vectors, eliminating the need to train separate LoRA adapters per task; reduces storage to 1% of original LoRA while matching or exceeding reconstruction quality.

nodes.label: Conditional Variational Autoencoder for LoRA Generation
nodes.rationale: CVAE encoder maps (LoRA parameter, task vector) pairs to latent z; decoder reconstructs LoRA parameters conditioned on z and task vector; trained with ELBO combining reconstruction and KL divergence terms. Uses 12-layer 1D CNN architecture. Task-conditioned generation allows multi-task LoRA parameter sharing.
nodes.norm_label: conditional variational autoencoder for lora generation

nodes.label: Task Vector Extraction via LLM/LVLM Hidden States
nodes.rationale: Task vectors are derived by averaging the hidden states at the last token of the last layer of a fine-tuned LLM/LVLM over task-specific samples; chosen because last-layer last-token representations capture high-level semantic features and form discriminative clusters per task category.
nodes.norm_label: task vector extraction via llm/lvlm hidden states

nodes.label: In-Context Meta-Learning for Parameter Generation
nodes.rationale: Combines ICL with meta-learning so the CVAE generator can model cross-task correlations and parameter distributions without storing raw datasets; enables task mapping between task descriptions and LoRA weight distributions.

nodes.label: COND P-DIFF (Conditional LoRA Parameter Generation)
nodes.author: Xiaolong Jin et al.

nodes.label: Model Soup (Weight Averaging)
nodes.author: Wortsman et al., 2022

nodes.label: A Modern Self-Referential Weight Matrix That Learns to Modify Itself
nodes.author: Kazuki Irie, Imanol Schlag, Robert Csordas, Jurgen Schmidhuber
nodes.norm_label: a modern self-referential weight matrix that learns to modify itself

nodes.label: Self-Referential Weight Matrix (SRWM) Mechanism
nodes.rationale: SRWM learns to generate key/value patterns and self-invented learning rates via outer products and the delta update rule, rapidly modifying its own weight matrix at runtime. Only initial weights are trained by gradient descent; all subsequent weight changes are driven by the self-referential dynamics. This collapses hierarchical FWP levels into a single self-modifying unit.

nodes.label: Fast Weight Programmers (FWP)
nodes.author: Schmidhuber 1991-1993
nodes.rationale: FWPs use a slow NN to continuously modify/program the weights of a fast NN; the delta update rule (additive outer-product update) is the core mechanism. Linear Transformer equivalence established by Schlag et al. 2021.

nodes.label: Delta Update Rule for Weight Modification
nodes.rationale: The delta rule W_t = W_{t-1} + sigma(beta)*(v - v_bar) ⊗ phi(k) is used to additively update fast weights using outer products of key-value vectors, enabling rapid context-dependent weight modification without gradient descent.
nodes.norm_label: delta update rule for weight modification

nodes.label: Towards Scalable and Versatile Weight Space Learning (SANE)
nodes.author: Konstantin Schurholt, Michael W. Mahoney, Damian Borth
nodes.norm_label: towards scalable and versatile weight space learning (sane)

nodes.label: SANE: Sequential Autoencoder for Neural Embeddings
nodes.rationale: SANE overcomes prior hyper-representation limits by tokenizing model weights layer-by-layer and encoding subsequences (windows) rather than the full flattened weight vector; decouples tokenization from representation learning, enabling embeddings of much larger and architecturally varying NNs. Uses contrastive guidance and reconstruction loss, with haloing and batch-norm conditioning for stability.
nodes.norm_label: sane: sequential autoencoder for neural embeddings

nodes.label: Hyper-Representations for Neural Network Weight Spaces
nodes.author: Schurholt et al. 2021; 2022a
nodes.rationale: Hyper-representations learn a lower-dimensional embedding z from populations of trained NN models via an encoder-decoder architecture trained with reconstruction and contrastive loss. Prior work was limited to models of fixed size/architecture.
nodes.norm_label: hyper-representations for neural network weight spaces

nodes.label: Model Zoo Datasets for Weight Space Learning
nodes.rationale: SANE uses model zoos: CNN zoos (MNIST, SVHN, CIFAR-10, STL-10 with ~2.5k-12k params) and ResNet-18 zoos (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet with ~12M params); ResNet zoos are 3 orders of magnitude larger than all prior hyper-representation model zoos.
nodes.norm_label: model zoo datasets for weight space learning

nodes.label: WeightWatcher Weight Analysis Metrics
nodes.author: Martin et al., 2021
nodes.rationale: WW metrics include log spectral norm log(||W||_inf) and weighted alpha (power law fit to empirical spectral density); used to validate that SANE embeddings capture similar global model quality signals.

nodes.label: Weight Space Representation Learning via Neural Field Adaptation
nodes.author: Zhuoqian Yang, Mathieu Salzmann, Sabine Susstrunk
nodes.norm_label: weight space representation learning via neural field adaptation

nodes.label: Multiplicative LoRA (mLoRA) for Neural Fields
nodes.rationale: Standard additive LoRA (W' = W + BA) introduces entanglement in neural fields by injecting new signal components into already-entangled feature mixtures. Multiplicative LoRA (W' = W ⊙ BA) instead scales existing features, preserving channel structure and avoiding further entanglement. This aligns with modulation mechanisms in generative neural fields and resolves internal permutation symmetry once external symmetry is broken by a shared base model.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Masking for Permutation Symmetry Breaking
nodes.rationale: Internal symmetry in LoRA factors (permuting r rank dimensions) is addressed by randomly freezing sqrt(d_out) entries per row of all A matrices; frozen positions are shared across instances and training runs, collapsing the GL(r)-fold equivalence class for each represented function. For mLoRA, frozen entries are zeroed out (removing rank components), which avoids weight entanglement unlike large-variance freezing in additive LoRA.
nodes.norm_label: asymmetric masking for permutation symmetry breaking

nodes.label: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs / Neural Fields)
nodes.rationale: INRs parameterize signals as continuous functions via neural networks, enabling resolution-independent, modality-agnostic representations. Using INR weights directly as data representations is motivated by their ability to encode diverse modalities in a unified architecture, but permutation symmetry of weights makes direct use challenging.

nodes.label: Diffusion Transformer on LoRA Weight Representations
nodes.rationale: A hierarchical LoRA layer encoder treats each rank component pair (a_i, b_i) as a token; vector-level positional encodings capture rank dimension indices and multi-head attention models intra-layer rank interactions; layer-level PE captures cross-layer relationships. This respects the paired structure of low-rank decomposition to enable generative modeling of weight spaces.
nodes.norm_label: diffusion transformer on lora weight representations

nodes.label: HyperDiffusion (Weight-Space Diffusion Baseline)
nodes.author: Erkon et al., 2023
nodes.rationale: HyperDiffusion trains a diffusion transformer over flattened MLP weights for implicit neural field generation; used as SOTA baseline in mLoRA experiments. mLoRA-Asym substantially outperforms HyperDiffusion on 2D FFHQ and 3D ShapeNet generation tasks.

nodes.label: Warping the Space: Weight Space Rotation for Class-Incremental Few-Shot Learning (WaRP)
nodes.author: Do-Yeon Kim, Dong-Jun Han, Jun Seo, Jaekyun Moon
nodes.norm_label: warping the space: weight space rotation for class-incremental few-shot learning (warp)

nodes.label: WaRP: Weight Space Rotation Process
nodes.rationale: WaRP reparameterizes weight matrix W using an arbitrary orthonormal basis B = {K_ij} constructed from unitary matrices V, U (via SVD of activation covariance). Due to low-rankness of activations, most directions in the new basis are flat (near-zero effect on output), so freezing a few important parameters in the new space preserves prior class knowledge while finetuning on new classes. Key insight: previous knowledge is broadly distributed in the standard basis but can be compacted to a few parameters in the WaRP basis.

nodes.label: Class-Incremental Few-Shot Learning (CIFSL)
nodes.rationale: CIFSL requires incrementally learning new classes with only a few training samples while preventing catastrophic forgetting of old classes; storage/privacy constraints prevent replaying old samples. Prior work addresses forgetting via parameter freezing (FSLL) or flat-minima pretraining (F2M), but WaRP addresses both via weight space reparameterization.

nodes.label: Low-Rankness Property of Neural Network Activations
nodes.author: Suzuki et al. 2020b; Wang et al. 2021
nodes.rationale: Deep neural network activations empirically exhibit low-rankness: singular values of activation covariance decrease rapidly, meaning inputs are concentrated on a low-dimensional subspace. WaRP exploits this by constructing a basis aligned with the dominant singular directions, so most basis directions are flat.
nodes.norm_label: low-rankness property of neural network activations

nodes.label: Weight-Space Linear Recurrent Neural Networks (WARP model)
nodes.author: Roussel Desmond Nzoyem, Nawid Keshtmand, Enrique Crespo Fernandez, Idriss Tsayem, Raul Santos-Rodriguez, David A.W. Barton, Tom Deakin
nodes.norm_label: weight-space linear recurrent neural networks (warp model)

nodes.label: WARP: Weight-space Adaptive Recurrent Prediction
nodes.rationale: WARP uses an auxiliary MLP ('root network') as the hidden state; its weights theta_t evolve via linear recurrence theta_t = A*theta_{t-1} + B*Delta_x_t, driven by input differences rather than raw inputs (inspired by continuous-time RNN theory). Decoding is non-linear (MLP applied to coordinates), combining linear recurrence efficiency (parallel scan) with expressivity from non-linear decoding. Enables gradient-free test-time adaptation and in-context learning as the root network adapts to context via weight-space dynamics.

nodes.label: Neural Network Weights as RNN Hidden State
nodes.rationale: WARP parametrizes RNN hidden state as the flattened weights of an auxiliary neural network; this high-dimensional representation enables infinite-capacity memory and non-linear decoding while maintaining the hardware efficiency of linear recurrence. Self-decoding (theta_t decodes itself) significantly reduces parameter count.
nodes.norm_label: neural network weights as rnn hidden state

nodes.label: Symmetries in Weight Space Learning: To Retain or Remove?
nodes.author: Anonymous (ICLR 2026 submission)
nodes.norm_label: symmetries in weight space learning: to retain or remove?

nodes.label: Theoretical Framework for Parameter Symmetries in Weight Space Learning
nodes.rationale: The paper proves that removing parameter symmetries (quotienting out equivalence classes) can compromise universality of weight-space learning: zeroth-order meta-regressors inherit all symmetries (safe to quotient), but higher-order features (k>=2) such as sensitivity/Hessian-based properties are only invariant to orthogonal transformations O(r), not the full GL_r(R) symmetry group of LoRA. Thus blindly applying invariant architectures can make certain weight-space tasks unsolvable. Symmetry handling should be task-specific.
nodes.norm_label: theoretical framework for parameter symmetries in weight space learning

nodes.label: LoRA Weight Space Symmetry Analysis
nodes.rationale: In LoRA, any invertible C in GL_r(R) maps (A,B) to (C^{-1}A, C^T B), preserving the end-to-end function. For zeroth-order weight-space learning this full GL_r symmetry is present; for sensitivity-based (Hessian-trace) features only orthogonal C in O(r) preserve the feature; for coordinate-specific (partial derivative) features no nontrivial symmetry is preserved. This stratification is the main theoretical result.

nodes.label: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)
nodes.author: Hu et al., 2021
nodes.rationale: LoRA parameterizes weight updates as W = W_0 + A^T B with low-rank A,B (rank r << p); reduces fine-tuning parameters drastically. Its weight space has GL_r(R) symmetry: (C^{-1}A, C^T B) encodes the same function for any invertible C.

nodes.label: Permutation Symmetry in Neural Network Weight Spaces
nodes.rationale: Functionally identical neural networks can occupy vastly different parameter space locations due to neuron reordering (permutation symmetry), making the weight distribution multi-modal and difficult to learn. External symmetries (from base neuron permutations) and internal symmetries (within LoRA rank dimensions) both require mitigation for effective weight space representation learning.
nodes.norm_label: permutation symmetry in neural network weight spaces

hyperedges.label: LoRA Ecosystem: Vanilla to Adaptive to Generated
hyperedges.rationale: These four concepts form a progression in LoRA sophistication: vanilla LoRA (uniform low-rank) -> asymmetry insight (A/B play different roles) -> AdaLoRA (adaptive rank via SVD importance) -> DnD (zero-shot LoRA generation from prompts). Each stage addresses a limitation of the previous.

hyperedges.label: Weight Space Composition Triangle
hyperedges.rationale: These papers and concepts form a coherent research program on composing models in weight space: task arithmetic establishes the framework and identifies disentanglement as prerequisite; TIES-Merging fixes sign conflicts that break naive composition; AWE adaptively tunes interpolation for few-shot settings. Together they advance the thesis that weight space supports systematic model combination.

hyperedges.label: Symmetry-Aware Architecture Understanding
hyperedges.rationale: These concepts and papers form a theory-to-application chain: functional symmetries provide the abstract theory of what transformations preserve neural network behavior; neural DAG automorphisms formalize these symmetries for arbitrary architectures; parameter graphs provide the practical representation; GMN implements equivariant processing; the survey synthesizes these into the WSU component of its taxonomy.

hyperedges.label: LoRA symmetry handling for weight-space generation
hyperedges.description: LoRA's GL_r symmetry and permutation symmetry are the core obstacles to using LoRA weights as data; multiplicative LoRA with asymmetric masking addresses both internal and external symmetries to produce structured, learnable weight spaces.

hyperedges.label: Multi-task LoRA generation via task vectors and CVAE
hyperedges.description: ICM-LoRA's three-stage pipeline: task vectors condition the CVAE, which is trained via in-context meta-learning to capture cross-task correlations; together they enable single-generator multi-task LoRA parameter synthesis.

hyperedges.label: Weight-space hidden state enables gradient-free adaptation
hyperedges.description: WARP's weight-space linear RNN unifies the fast weight programmer paradigm with weight-space learning: the auxiliary network's weights serve as the hidden state, updated via linear recurrence with input differences, enabling gradient-free test-time adaptation.
